Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: Digital civil register (Madania system) fully deployed nationwide since 2005, central database hosted by CNI, interconnected 350+ offices.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the official Centre National de l'Informatique (CNI) page describing Madania as Tunisia's centralised national civil status system, electronically exchanging records with municipalities, commercial sites and social security funds. Corroborated by a 2024 ID4Africa country presentation confirming the system (in operation since 2004) remains the national civil status backbone, and by the original 2020 CRVS Systems Centre of Excellence report describing full digitisation and interconnection of registration offices. The originally cited sources are relevant and support the score. As this is the maximum code on the scale, flagged for human review per the top-of-scale escalation rule, though evidence is authoritative and consistent across sources through 2024.
revised_comments: Tunisia's national civil status system, Madania, is a fully digitised and centralised civil register operated by the Centre National de l'Informatique, interconnecting several hundred municipal and commercial registration sites nationwide. The system enables online issuance of civil status documents regardless of place of registration and electronic exchange of records with the national social security funds, and has been operational since the mid-2000s.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Birth registration 99.9-100% complete since 2001; death >95%; proxy for population coverage.
revision_notes: Confirmed via World Bank WDI (SP.REG.BRTH.ZS), whose most recent data point for Tunisia (2018) shows 100% birth registration completeness. Corroborated by a UNICEF Africa Birth Registration Brochure (October 2022), which still cites Tunisia's most recent survey (MICS 2018) at 100%, and by the original UNFPA/INS Knowledge Brief (2021) confirming completeness of 99.9-100% since 2001, consistent across rural/urban and male/female breakdowns. No survey more recent than 2018 was identified; MICS/DHS-style household surveys remain the standard data source and none newer has been published. The originally cited sources are relevant and support the score. As this is the maximum code on the scale, flagged for human review per the top-of-scale escalation rule, though evidence is authoritative and converges across three independent sources.
revised_comments: Birth registration completeness in Tunisia is effectively universal, standing at 100% according to World Bank and UNICEF data (MICS 2018), with completeness above 99% recorded consistently since 2001 across rural and urban areas and by sex. This near-total civil registration coverage is used as the standard proxy for population register coverage.
